title: Trace the attacker
briefing: Security wants the IP address behind the most failed logins in /var/log/auth.log.
3,000 lines. A pipeline will crack it in seconds.
tips: `grep -oE 'PATTERN'` prints only the matching part; then sort | uniq -c | sort -rn ranks.
objective: Find the IP address responsible for the most failed logins in /var/log/auth.log, and write just that IP into ~/attacker_ip.txt.
hints: Keep only failed-login lines, then extract just the IP from each and count them.
grep 'Failed password' /var/log/auth.log, then `grep -oE '[0-9.]+' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` — the top line is your IP.
One answer: grep the failures, extract IPs, rank them; then  echo 203.0.113.66 > ~/attacker_ip.txt
solution:
grep 'Failed password' /var/log/auth.log | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -1
echo 203.0.113.66 > ~/attacker_ip.txt
explanation: `grep -oE` prints only the matched substring, so you can pull IPs, emails or tokens straight out of noisy logs, then rank them with the sort|uniq|sort pipeline. This is real incident triage.
